One-block probability. A proper signed-bit span has rank equal to its number of distinct bit variables. From a block of rank above \(2h\), choose \(r\) distinct variables and their prescribed mismatch-zero values. Let the affected pigeon rows have \(k_1,\ldots,k_w\) chosen bits, with \(1\le k_i\le\ell\) and \(\sum_i k_i=r\). If the block has no constant-one input after restriction, every fixed affected row must receive a label matching its chosen bit pattern. A row with \(k_i\) prescribed bits has at most \(n2^{-k_i}\) compatible outside labels.

For a specified subset \(A\) of the affected rows that are live, its probability is at most \(p_{\rm live}^{|A|}\), by sampling without replacement. Conditional on the live set, the other \(t=w-|A|\) affected rows get distinct uniform outside labels. Their compatibility probability is at most
\[ \frac{\prod_{i\notin A}n2^{-k_i}}{(q)_t} \le\prod_{i\notin A}\alpha\,2^{-k_i}, \]

The accuracy is compatible with compact-clause packing, since \(h\ge\ell\). If the whole supplied family is one-level signed-bit input, a polylogarithmic-degree refutation would therefore yield a degree-\(D\) refutation of \(\mathcal Q_N\), contradicting its \(N/2+1\) PC barrier for large \(n\). This is a binary literal-family theorem; original level-one MOD-containing inputs can be general affine forms, and later levels remain separate.

excerpts.text: Hakoniemi–Limaye–Tzameret, “Hard CNF Instances for Ideal Proof Systems,” v1 (6 May 2026) studies roABP-IPS and states CNF lower bounds. Its Proposition 21 gives a functional-PHP upper-bound argument using the Boolean equations for \(y_1,\ldots,y_n\) and \(n+1-\sum_k y_k=0\), treating that subsystem as unsatisfiable. We checked the displayed statement and proof on PDF pages 27–28. Their main CNF lower-bound proof was not audited or applied here.

Exact field check. On Boolean inputs the sum is an integer Hamming weight \(r\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\), interpreted in the field. In characteristic zero, or prime characteristic \(p>n+1\), \(n+1-r\) cannot vanish. If \(p\le n+1\), take \(r\) to be the least nonnegative residue of \(n+1\) modulo \(p\); then \(r\le n\), and any vector with \(r\) ones is a model. Thus the displayed subset-sum step does not establish the upper bound over fixed small prime fields. This countermodel is for that intermediate subsystem, not for FPHP. It neither disproves every possible roABP upper bound nor challenges the paper's main CNF theorem.

The 2021 algebraic-proof-complexity paper and Elbaz–Govindasamy–Lu–Tzameret (2025), v1 were screened for model/background definitions only; no PHP lower-bound theorem was imported from them.

excerpts.text: Existence with \(v=64(r+1)\). Choose each column independently and uniformly from \(\mathbb F_2^r\). For each fixed nonzero \(\lambda\), its codeword consists of independent fair bits. If \(\epsilon_i\in\{-1,1\}\) are their signed versions, then \(\mathbb E e^{t\sum_i\epsilon_i}=(\cosh t)^v\le e^{vt^2/2}\). The inequality follows by integrating \(\tanh t\le t\). Markov's inequality with \(t=1/4\), in both tails, bounds the chance that the weight lies outside the required interval by \(2e^{-v/32}\). A union bound over nonzero \(\lambda\) gives failure probability at most
\[ 2^{r+1}e^{-v/32} =\exp\big((r+1)(\log2-2)\big)<1. \tag{CODE-existence} \]

Thus a suitable matrix exists with \(O(r^2)\) bits of description. This is a probabilistic existence proof, not a claim of a deterministic polynomial-time verifier for arbitrary large \(r\). The finite witnesses below explicitly enumerate their codeword weights.
Every variable order has a middle cut into two sets of \(v/2\) variables. Combining this lemma with (CODE-cut) gives ROABP width at least \(2^{r-2}\) for \(f_b\) in every order.

\[ \frac{\binom{v-r_*+k}{k}}{\binom mk\ell^k} =\prod_{j=0}^{k-1} \left(1- \frac{h(k+1)-(\ell+1)j}{v-\ell j}\right) \le \exp\left(-\frac{hk^2}{2m\ell}\right). \tag{RANK-dimension} \]

The simultaneous packed/high-rank map and the weighted PC replay are unchanged: low coefficient degree is at most \(k\), high products become \(1-f\), and every weighted axiom image fits \(k\) times its original degree plus \(k\). The old consequence \(f\) would be derived through \(B\), contradicting row-linear separation and old stability under the displayed conditions. This refines the earlier sufficient parameter choice; it does not assume logarithmic \(h\) or polylogarithmic \(D\) in the finite statement.
